title: Trust at First Click? User Acceptance of Digital Consent Interfaces Among Users of Psychiatric Services
summary:
Health apps and wearable devices collect valuable information that can support medical care. However, it is often unclear how and with whom this data can be shared securely. This study tests a new digital consent management system called the Standard Health Consent (SHC). The SHC allows people to decide for themselves which of their health data they want to share for treatment or research purposes.

Participants receiving psychiatric care at the University Hospital Dresden will use the Mood Tracker App for four weeks to record their daily mood. Through the SHC, they can manage their consent settings and decide with whom and for what purpose their data may be shared. The study evaluates how understandable, trustworthy, and user-friendly this new digital consent system is in a clinical setting.
conditions: The study targets individuals who use psychiatric services and examines the acceptance of a digital consent system (Standard Health Consent, SHC) for managing health data.

interventions.name: Users of psychiatric services who will use the web-based Mood Tracker App for four weeks to record their daily mood (adapted PHQ-2 questionnaire). The app is linked to the Standard Health Consent (SHC), which allows participants to decide whether and for what purposes their health data may be shared

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Users of psychiatric services over the age of 18 at the three recruitment locations: Early Detection Center “Früh dran,” Psychiatric Outpatient Clinic, Center for Mental Health: Day clinic for young people in Dresden who are suspected of having a mental illness or who contact a participating center themselves or are referred with corresponding suspected diagnoses.
- Declaration of consent to participate in the study
- Sufficient knowledge of German
- Access to a smartphone, tablet, or computer
- Subsequent treatment by an approving healthcare provider
Exclusion criteria:
- Inability to give informed consent
- Acute psychiatric or other conditions that would prevent safe and meaningful use of the app.
- Vulnerable groups (children, individuals who cannot give consent, emergency patients, pregnant women/nursing mothers)
